title: Come and see (John 1:29–39)
hookLine: John points, two disciples follow, and Jesus asks what seek you

lines: A LINE NOW SAID AT MASS.
cards: Bethania, beyond the Jordan. John is baptizing there when he sees a man walking toward him, and he points.
What he says next is a line the priest repeats at Mass just before Communion, lifting the host: behold the Lamb of God. It didn't come from a council or a liturgist. It came from a riverbank.
Today, that line, and what two people do the moment they hear it.

teach.b: John the Baptist sees Jesus coming and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world." Lamb of God is a strange thing to call a man.

Readers hear in it the Passover lamb, whose blood marked the doors in Egypt, the lambs offered every day in the temple, and Isaiah's servant, led as a sheep to the slaughter. John packs all of that into one name.
The next day he says it again, and two of his own disciples hear him, leave him, and follow Jesus.
Jesus turns, sees them trailing behind, and speaks his first words in this Gospel: "What seek you?" Not who are you, not what do you believe. What are you looking for?
They answer with a question of their own: Rabbi, where do you live?
And he says: "Come and see." No sermon, no test, just an invitation to come along and look.
They came, saw where he abode, and stayed with him that day; John even remembers the hour, about the tenth hour, late in the afternoon. One of the two was Andrew.
The other is never named; some readers have thought it was the writer himself, remembering the afternoon his life turned. The Church keeps John's pointing finger at the center of the Mass.
The Lamb of God is sung while the bread is broken, and then the priest lifts the host, points as John pointed, and says: behold.

how: At every Mass the Lamb of God (Agnus Dei) is sung or said while the priest breaks the host, and just before Communion he holds it up and repeats John the Baptist's words, behold the Lamb of God.

games.q: you're one of John the Baptist's disciples. he points at a man walking by and says: behold the Lamb of God. what do you do?
o: follow the man down the road.
games.why: two of them simply follow. Jesus turns, asks what seek you, and says come and see. they stay with him that day.

practice: Imagine someone turning around on a path and asking you, kindly and directly: what are you looking for?
Let the real answer come up, not the one you think you should give: peace, a person, rest, or I don't know, which is an answer too.
If you pray, tell God plainly what you're seeking; if you don't, just let yourself hear your own answer.

wordCard.voice: Agnus Dei. The Latin for Lamb of God, John the Baptist's name for Jesus at the Jordan, sung again at every Mass before Communion. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: lamb of God (John 1:29); in Latin, Agnus Dei, the words sung at Mass.

carryVoice: Your line: what seek you. His first question in this Gospel, still asked. That's day four hundred ninety-four.
